PA.III.A.K1.why: PHAK ch14 Airport Operations covers radio communications and where facility frequencies are published; AIM 9-1 Types of Charts Available covers the Chart Supplement and sectional panels that list them

PA.III.A.K2.why: AIM 4-2 is Radio Communications Phraseology and Techniques; PHAK ch14 Airport Operations teaches basic ATC communication procedure

PA.III.A.K3.why: ATC traffic control light signals are tabulated in AIM 4-3 Airport Operations and repeated in PHAK ch14

PA.III.A.K4.why: AIM 4-1 Services Available to Pilots covers transponder and ADS-B Out operation and code assignment; PHAK ch14 covers transponder use with ATC

PA.III.A.K5.why: AIM 6-4 is Two-way Radio Communications Failure; PHAK ch14 covers lost communication procedure and light signal acknowledgment

PA.III.A.K6.why: PHAK ch14 covers the radio and audio panel equipment involved; PHAK ch07 Aircraft Systems covers the electrical and avionics failures that silence it

PA.III.A.K7.why: AIM 4-1 covers radar traffic information service and terminal radar service for VFR aircraft; PHAK ch14 covers radar assistance to VFR pilots

PA.III.A.K8.why: AIM 7-7 Safety, Accident, and Hazard Reports states the NTSB Part 830 immediate notification and reporting requirements

PA.III.A.K9.why: AIM 2-1 Airport Lighting Aids includes the Runway Status Light System; PHAK ch14 covers runway lighting the pilot sees

PA.III.A.R1.why: RMH ch6 Threat and Error Management treats miscommunication as a communication error to trap; PHAK ch02 ADM covers communication as a resource management skill

PA.III.A.R2.why: AIM 6-3 Distress and Urgency Procedures covers when and how to declare an emergency; RMH ch8 Aeronautical Decision-Making in Flight covers making that call in the air

PA.III.A.R3.why: element is archived, nothing to map

PA.III.A.R4.why: AIM 4-2 prescribes standard phraseology and explains the hazard created by nonstandard transmissions

PA.III.A.S1.why: PHAK ch14 Airport Operations covers selecting and tuning the correct frequency for the facility in use

PA.III.A.S2.why: AIM 4-2 is the phraseology and technique reference this element cites by name

PA.III.A.S3.why: AIM 4-2 covers contact and readback procedure; AIM 5-5 Pilot/Controller Roles and Responsibilities sets the duty to comply with ATC instructions

PA.III.B.K1.why: AIM 4-3 covers towered and nontowered airport operations, AFH ch8 Airport Traffic Patterns covers flying them, PHAK ch14 gives the ground school treatment

PA.III.B.K2.why: AFH ch8 Airport Traffic Patterns covers pattern entry and selection; AIM 4-3 gives runway and pattern selection at nontowered fields

PA.III.B.K3.why: right-of-way rules are 14 CFR 91.113 and no single chapter covers them better than the whole handbook

PA.III.B.K4.why: AIM 4-1 covers ATIS and automated airport information services; PHAK ch13 Aviation Weather Services covers ASOS and AWOS broadcasts

PA.III.B.R1.why: AFH ch8 covers see-and-avoid and clearing turns in the pattern; AIM 4-3 covers the self-announce and traffic advisory practice that prevents pattern conflicts

PA.III.B.R2.why: RMH ch6 Threat and Error Management covers distraction, task saturation, and loss of situational awareness; PHAK ch02 ADM covers task prioritization and SRM

PA.III.B.R3.why: AIM 7-4 is Wake Turbulence; PHAK ch12 Weather Theory covers wind shear and microbursts near the airport

PA.III.B.S1.why: AIM 2-3 is Airport Marking Aids and Signs, AIM 2-1 is Airport Lighting Aids, PHAK ch14 covers runway and taxiway identification

PA.III.B.S2.why: AFH ch8 gives the recommended traffic pattern procedures; AIM 4-3 gives recommended entry, departure, and sequencing

PA.III.B.S3.why: AFH ch7 Ground Reference Maneuvers teaches wind drift correction to hold a ground track, applied to the rectangular course in AFH ch8

PA.III.B.S4.why: AFH ch8 Airport Traffic Patterns covers keeping the runway in sight and oriented on each leg

PA.III.B.S5.why: AFH ch8 sets pattern altitude and airspeed; AFH ch4 Energy Management covers holding altitude and airspeed to tolerance

PA.III.B.S6.why: AFH ch8 covers spacing and sequencing behind other traffic; AIM 4-3 covers traffic advisory practice and pattern sequencing
